info.stanceWidth: Distance between your feet when you take guard. Wider gives stability, narrower allows quicker movement.
info.backliftAngle: How high you lift the bat before the downswing. Higher backlift generates more power but needs better timing.
info.headPosition: Where your head is relative to your body at the moment of contact. Staying still and over the ball improves control.
info.frontKneeAngle: Bend in your front knee at impact. A braced front leg transfers power; too bent absorbs energy.
info.batSwingPlane: The angle your bat travels through during the shot. A straighter plane means more consistent contact.
info.followThroughExtension: How fully you extend after hitting. Full follow-through means committed shot-making.
info.releaseHeight: How high your arm is when you let go of the ball. Higher release = more bounce.
info.actionType: Whether your body faces side-on, front-on, or mixes both during delivery. Mixed actions can increase injury risk.
info.estimatedSpeed: Approximate ball speed based on your body segment velocities during delivery.
info.seamAngle: Orientation of the wrist at release — indicates whether you're bowling seam-up, cross-seam, or angled.
info.runUpRhythm: Consistency of your stride pattern in the run-up. Rhythmic approach = better timing at the crease.
info.injuryRisk: Flags for biomechanical patterns linked to common bowling injuries (back, knee, shoulder).
